messages:
From: Michael Zhou <michael.zhou@findata.ai>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai; ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: dana@app-lation.com
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 15:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick demo follow-up and compatibility questions

Alex / Ben —

Really appreciate the demo today. A couple of high-level items I want to capture from our end before we commit to the next trial:

- Competitive delta: our infra team wants a concise, quantified comparison (latency P50/P95, token cost per 1k, model parity on our key prompts) between Redwood and the hyperscalers we evaluated (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI). The demo highlighted promising latency numbers but we need hard numbers against our baseline.
- OpenAI API compatibility: we run a thin-compat layer today. Any SDK swap or minor API discrepancy will multiply our QA overhead. Can you outline exact compatibility gaps we should expect (auth, streaming semantics, function-calling, error codes)?
- Prompt diffs: we saw some response tone/format differences on our reimbursement and policy prompts — can you run an automated diff suite we shared? (I attached a small sample.)

Next steps we propose: a 2-week sandbox where we (FinData) run a side-by-side test with 3 focused workload buckets (short transactional prompts, long-context summarization, streaming chat). We need an MAP and a minimal action plan with owners.

I attached the sample prompt bundle and the call recording request. If you can share the MAP by EOD Monday (your time), we can align internal schedules.

Thanks,
Michael
Director of Platform Engineering
FinData

From: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
To: Michael Zhou <michael.zhou@findata.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: quantified deltas vs hyperscalers & proposed SDK transition plan

Michael — thanks for the clear ask and the prompt bundle. Good call capturing the three workload buckets. Below is a short post-call recap and a proposed MAP for a 2-week sandbox plus a recommended SDK transition approach.

Recap (what we heard)
- You need quantified performance/cost deltas vs AWS/Azure/OpenAI for specific prompt classes.
- Minimizing changes for your engineering team is a hard requirement — the OpenAI-compatible surface counts a lot.
- Prompt parity checks should be automated and reproducible; you shared a representative sample which is perfect.

Proposed 2-week sandbox MAP (high level)
1) Kickoff (Day 0): agree test corpus + success metrics (owner: Michael).
2) Baseline run (Days 1–2): FinData runs current provider to capture P50/P95, token counts, and failure modes (owner: FinData).
3) Redwood run (Days 3–7): Redwood runs identical workloads on a hosted sandbox instance (owner: Redwood engineering — Alex).
4) Diff analysis (Days 8–10): automated prompt-delta report + manual triage where diffs exceed thresholds (owner: Redwood QA + FinData SME).
5) SDK swap smoke (Day 11): staged SDK swap in FinData dev environment — minimal wrapper to keep call shape identical; run 50% of short transactional traffic (owner: FinData + Redwood SE).
6) Review & decision (Day 14): joint review of metric deltas and recommended sticking points.

Success metrics (examples)
- Latency: P95 within +35% of baseline for short transactional prompts.
- Quality: <= 3% actionable output divergence on critical prompts (measured by diff suite).
- Cost: per-token cost delta benchmarked for your monthly token envelope.

Compatibility notes (short):
- Auth: Redwood supports API keys and token-scoped keys; OAuth flows differ from Azure AD but we can support a proxy.
- Streaming: Redwood supports chunked streaming identical to OpenAI's chunk marker semantics, but we return an additional final control frame for traceability; client should tolerate that final frame (we can toggle).
- Function calling: We support JSON schema-driven function calling; there is a minor difference in error wrapping. We'll provide a shim in the SDK to normalize error types.
- Error codes & rate limit headers: slightly different header names, full mapping included in the attached MAP.

Proposed SDK transition approach:
- Provide a lightweight SDK adapter package (open-source) that aliases OpenAI call shapes to Redwood SDK calls. This adapter will: translate auth headers, normalize streaming frames, and map error codes.
- Rolling swap plan: shadow traffic -> canary (5%) -> 25% -> full swap over 48–72 hours with automatic fallback.

Attachments: MAP_v1.xlsx (action plan + owners), demo-recording-20261119.mp4 (recording of today's session).

I'll sync with Ben and Marissa on pricing and infra constraints; Ben, Marissa — flag any items that should change in the MAP. Michael, can we lock kickoff for Monday 23 Nov at 10am PT?

Cheers,
Alex Martinez
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Looping in quick internal alignment:
- Pricing: recommend offering a 3-month pilot price commitment (flat monthly spend) with a 10% pilot credit if FinData signs the MAP by Mon EOD. That gives them predictable spend while we collect metrics.
- Infra: for the sandbox, recommend reserved dedicated instances with pre-warmed KV cache for long-context tests — reduces cold-start noise. Estimate added infra delta ~ $1.2k/week (we can absorb 50% for pilot).
- Risks: prompt parity on policy-related prompts may need prompt engineering adjustments; schedule a 30-min triage slot during the diff analysis window.

If that sounds good, Alex, add pricing rows to the MAP and flag a contact for procurement.

—Ben
Head of Revenue, Redwood Inference
